abstract: We study revenue optimization learning algorithms for repeated posted-price auctions where a seller interacts with a single strategic buyer that holds a fixed private valuation for a good and seeks to maximize his cumulative discounted surplus. We propose a novel algorithm that never decreases offered prices and has a tight strategic regret bound of $\Theta(\log\log T)$. This result closes the open research question on the existence of a no-regret horizon-independent weakly consistent pricing. We also show that the property of non-decreasing prices is nearly necessary for a weakly consistent algorithm to be a no-regret one.
title: Weakly Consistent Optimal Pricing Algorithms in Repeated Posted-Price Auctions with Strategic Buyer

abstract: Detecting anomalies with limited supervision is challenging due to the scarcity of labeled anomalies, which often fail to capture the diversity of abnormal behaviors. We propose Weakly Supervised Anomaly Detection via Dual-Tailed Kernel (WSAD-DT), a novel framework that learns robust latent representations to distinctly separate anomalies from normal samples under weak supervision. WSAD-DT introduces two centroids—one for normal samples and one for anomalies—and leverages a dual-tailed kernel scheme: a light-tailed kernel to compactly model in-class points and a heavy-tailed kernel to main- tain a wider margin against out-of-class instances. To preserve intra-class diversity, WSAD-DT in- corporates kernel-based regularization, encouraging richer representations within each class. Furthermore, we devise an ensemble strategy that partition unlabeled data into diverse subsets, while sharing the limited labeled anomalies among these partitions to maximize their impact. Empirically, WSAD-DT achieves state-of-the-art performance on several challenging anomaly detection benchmarks, outperforming leading ensemble-based methods such as XGBOD.

summary.idea: Learn normal and anomaly centers with complementary light- and heavy-tailed kernels, preserve within-class diversity through regularization, and share scarce anomaly labels across an ensemble of data partitions.
summary.limitations: The abstract does not identify the benchmarks, label budgets, or gain sizes, and does not establish detection of anomaly types absent from the evaluated settings.
summary.problem: A few labeled anomalies may represent only a small fraction of possible abnormal behavior, making weakly supervised anomaly detection difficult.
summary.results: WSAD-DT reports state-of-the-art results on several anomaly-detection benchmarks, outperforming leading ensemble approaches including XGBOD.
summary.tldr: Complementary kernel shapes and an ensemble strategy help make scarce anomaly labels more useful.

title: Weakly Supervised Anomaly Detection via Dual-Tailed Kernel

abstract: Many classification problems have the property that the only costly part of obtaining examples is the class label. This paper suggests a simple method for using distribution information contained in unlabeled examples to augment labeled examples in a supervised training framework. Empirical tests show that the technique de(cid:173) scribed in this paper can significantly improve the accuracy of a supervised learner when the learner is well below its asymptotic accuracy level.

summary.idea: Use the distributional information in unlabeled examples to augment supervised training on labeled data.
summary.limitations: The abstract does not describe the augmentation procedure, datasets, or numerical gains. Its reported benefit is conditional on the learner's low-data performance regime, not a guarantee that unlabeled data always helps.
summary.problem: In many classification tasks, examples are easy to collect but their labels are expensive, leaving useful information in a large unlabeled pool.
summary.results: Empirical tests show substantial accuracy improvements when the supervised learner is still far below the performance it approaches with abundant data.
summary.tldr: Unlabeled examples can improve a data-limited supervised learner by supplying information about the input distribution.

title: Using Unlabeled Data for Supervised Learning

abstract: Neural networks often learn to make predictions that overly rely on spurious corre- lation existing in the dataset, which causes the model to be biased. While previous work tackles this issue by using explicit labeling on the spuriously correlated attributes or presuming a particular bias type, we instead utilize a cheaper, yet generic form of human knowledge, which can be widely applicable to various types of bias. We first observe that neural networks learn to rely on the spurious correlation only when it is “easier” to learn than the desired knowledge, and such reliance is most prominent during the early phase of training. Based on the obser- vations, we propose a failure-based debiasing scheme by training a pair of neural networks simultaneously. Our main idea is twofold; (a) we intentionally train the first network to be biased by repeatedly amplifying its “prejudice”, and (b) we debias the training of the second network by focusing on samples that go against the prejudice of the biased network in (a). Extensive experiments demonstrate that our method significantly improves the training of network against various types of biases in both synthetic and real-world datasets. Surprisingly, our framework even occasionally outperforms the debiasing methods requiring explicit supervision of the spuriously correlated attributes.

summary.idea: Two networks learn together. One is deliberately encouraged to follow easy biases; the other emphasizes examples on which that biased network struggles, using its failures as a training signal.
summary.limitations: The approach is motivated by biases being easier to learn than the desired signal, especially early in training. The abstract does not establish that all relevant biases meet that condition or provide numerical gains.
summary.problem: Classifiers can exploit easy but misleading correlations instead of learning the intended visual or semantic signal. Many debiasing methods require explicit labels describing those correlations.
summary.results: Experiments across synthetic and real datasets improve performance under various biases, occasionally exceeding methods that receive explicit labels for spuriously correlated attributes.
summary.tldr: Use a deliberately biased model's failures to direct another model toward more reliable patterns.

title: Learning from Failure: De-biasing Classifier from Biased Classifier
